summary: Full read of 20 SEC whistleblower award orders (19 May - 2 Aug 2021). Adds 5 case rows: 4 denial rows (other claimants denied in the same orders, contested and uncontested) and 1 award row (Release No. 92164, Claimant 2, 2%; the existing combined row is suggested to become Claimant 1's 28%). Suggested corrections add to each existing award row how the claimant qualified, contests, reductions for reporting delay, the 30% presumption, waivers (late Form TCR, late WB-APP exempted under Section 36(a)) and internal-reporting facts. No statistics, new rules or new events; percentages, sanctions and names are redacted in most orders.

cases.summary: Award claim of Claimant 2 denied after contest: the staff never received or used the tip, which came months after the inquiry opened and was closed by the whistleblower office with "No Further Action".

cases.summary: Award of 2% to Claimant 2, who reported after a delay with information mostly already known from Claimant 1; aggregate award at the 30% maximum under the new presumption.

Rule 21F-6(c)(3): because Claimant 1 qualified for the presumption, the aggregate award is the statutory maximum (28% + 2%). Claimant 1's 28% award is the existing row for this order.

suggested_corrections.value: Exchange Act Release No. 91933, File No. 2021-50. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (May 19, 2021). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Amount as printed: "more than": lower bound. Award amount and percentage are as recommended by the Claims Review Staff and adopted by the Commission unless the order says otherwise. Award on a covered action (including administrative proceedings against individual respondents, treated as one) and a related action by another agency, a DOJ-type agreement deemed a related action under Rule 21F-4(d)(3)(i) (type redacted). Not contested. Tip prompted SEC and other-agency investigations of the company's conduct in one country; the company then reported similar problems in another region; the charges largely concerned regions outside the tip, so the nexus was weak and the percentage (redacted) reflects limited contribution.
Award on a covered and related action for a tip about one country that opened investigations; percentage limited because most charges concerned other regions.

Exchange Act Release No. 92037, File No. 2021-51. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (May 27, 2021). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Award amount as printed. Claimant 1. Not contested. The CRS first recommended a (redacted) percentage, then, after a later Commission step (redacted), recommended $4.2 million. Covered action combined several underlying investigations; Claimant 1's detailed, credible report caused staff to open one of them; met staff multiple times and identified key players. Claimant 2 (contested) and a third claimant (no response) denied (separate rows). Percentage redacted. Pages 2 and 4 are images (read by OCR).
Award for a detailed report that opened one of several investigations behind the action; two other claimants denied.

Exchange Act Release No. 92086, File No. 2021-54. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Orders (PDF)" (June 2, 2021). Separate award amounts per claimant in one order: this row is the amount stated for Claimant 1 (claimants numbered in the order the amounts appear). Amount as printed: "approximately". Claimant 1: award on a covered action and a related action by another agency (an agreement type deemed a related action under the amended rules; details redacted); same percentage in both (redacted). Not contested. Tip led to the opening of the SEC and other-agency investigations into a complex fraudulent scheme with tens of millions of dollars in ill-gotten gains; substantial assistance.
Larger award to the claimant whose tip opened SEC and other-agency investigations into a complex fraud; covered and related action.

Exchange Act Release No. 92086, File No. 2021-54. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Orders (PDF)" (June 2, 2021). Separate award amounts per claimant in one order: this row is the amount stated for Claimant 2 (claimants numbered in the order the amounts appear). Amount as printed: "approximately". Claimant 2: award on the same covered and related actions. Not contested. Information significantly contributed to the investigations, but reduced for unreasonable reporting delay (waited several years while the conduct continued). Form WB-APP arrived 18 days after the 90-day deadline; no "extraordinary circumstances" under Rule 21F-8(a), but the Commission used its Section 36(a) exemptive authority to excuse the deadline (undue hardship, significant contribution, unique obstacles). Percentage redacted.
Award to a second claimant despite a late application (deadline exempted under Section 36(a)); reduced for reporting delay of several years.

Exchange Act Release No. 92099, File No. 2021-55. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (June 3, 2021). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Amount as printed: "almost": upper bound. Award amount and percentage are as recommended by the Claims Review Staff and adopted by the Commission unless the order says otherwise. Rule 21F-9(e) waiver: no Form TCR within 30 days of first contacting the Commission, but filed within 30 days of learning of the requirement. Meaningful information advanced the investigation; continuing assistance; acted quickly. Footnote 6: later SEC actions with sanctions of $1 million or less may be treated as part of this covered action (Rule 21F-4(d)(2)). Percentage redacted; several redacted footnotes. Contest status not stated. No other claimants.
Award for information that advanced an investigation; late Form TCR excused under Rule 21F-9(e).

Exchange Act Release No. 92100, File No. 2021-56. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (June 3, 2021). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. The order gives no dollar amount; percentage stated: 30%. Maximum award under the Rule 21F-6(c) presumption. Tip caused staff to begin an examination (Rule 21F-4(c)(1)); Claimant (role redacted) spoke with staff and gave documents. The order says that because nothing has been collected, the 30% award would not result in any payment. Contest status not stated; no other claimants.
Maximum 30% award under the presumption for a tip that started an examination; nothing collected, so no payment.

Exchange Act Release No. 92101, File No. 2021-57. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (June 3, 2021). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Amount as printed: "over": lower bound. Award on a related action only (other authority redacted); Claimant had earlier received a (redacted) percentage award on the covered action. Information revealed an ongoing fraudulent scheme harming investors; several interviews; close nexus to the related-action charges. Sanctions used to satisfy related-action obligations not double counted. Percentage redacted; most of p. 2 redacted. No other claimants.
Related-action award to a claimant already paid on the covered action, for information revealing an ongoing fraud.

Exchange Act Release No. 92102, File No. 2021-58. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (June 3, 2021). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Amount as printed: "over": lower bound. Award on a covered and related action for revealing fraudulent conduct in a geographic area the SEC did not know about.

Exchange Act Release No. 92163, File No. 2021-59. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Orders (PDF)" (June 14, 2021). Whistleblowers awarded: 2. Amount as printed: "approximately". Award amount and percentage are as recommended by the Claims Review Staff and adopted by the Commission unless the order says otherwise. Two claimants with separate (redacted) percentages; the aggregate award is expected to give an initial combined payment of approximately $3 million based on anticipated collections. Neither contested. Amounts distributed to investors in the covered action treated as collected sanctions (footnote 1). Claimant 1 helped early to focus staff resources and theories; Claimant 2 helped uncover misappropriated funds and fraudulent transfers. The order gives no per-claimant split of the amount.
Separate awards to two claimants (combined about $3 million) who helped focus the investigation and trace misappropriated funds.

Exchange Act Release No. 92164, File No. 2021-60. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Orders (PDF)" (June 14, 2021). This row: Claimant 1, 28%. Claimant 2 (2%) is a separate row. Not contested. No dollar amount given; the statutory maximum would be less than $5 million. Rule 21F-6(c)(3): one claimant qualifying for the presumption makes the aggregate award 30%. Claimant 1 alerted authorities first, gave significant new information and substantial continuing assistance during investigation and litigation; no negative factors. Anonymous.

Exchange Act Release No. 92210, File No. 2021-61. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Order (PDF)" (June 21, 2021). Whistleblowers awarded: 1. Amount as printed: "nearly": upper bound. "Extraordinary assistance": hours of telephone interviews, more than 125 emails with staff, documents explained, key witnesses identified. Claimant took personal and professional risks by raising concerns internally. Claimants 2-4 denied (separate row). Percentage redacted.
Award for a tip that opened the investigation and extraordinary assistance; claimant had raised concerns internally at personal risk.

Exchange Act Release No. 92212, File No. 2021-62. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Orders (PDF)" (June 21, 2021). Claimant 1: "over $1,000,000" (lower bound). Claimant 1. Not contested. Detailed information about one respondent's conduct caused staff to open an investigation and played a critical role; substantial ongoing assistance. Also gets the same (redacted) percentage of sanctions in a separate pending administrative proceeding if $1 million or less is ordered there (Rule 21F-4(d)(2)). Two settled proceedings treated as one covered action. Percentage redacted.
Larger share to the claimant whose detailed tip opened one of two investigations behind the action and gave leads the joint claimants did not.

Exchange Act Release No. 92212, File No. 2021-62. Listed on the SEC Final Orders page as "Award Orders (PDF)" (June 21, 2021). Joint claimants (Claimants 2 and 3, as the order numbers them): joint award "over $270,000" (lower bound). Joint Claimants 2 and 3 (same counsel, joint application; paid 50% each unless they ask otherwise). They contested, seeking a larger share and not to be treated as joint; both rejected: their tip opened a separate investigation but covered only one respondent's misconduct, and staff developed the rest independently; the Commission had treated them as joint whistleblowers in an earlier award. Percentage redacted.
Joint award to two claimants whose tip opened a separate investigation; contest for a larger share and separate treatment rejected.
